svg.title: Three layers, each aimed at a different adversary
svg.desc: Three stacked bands running from dark to light, representing the three layers of everyday digital preparation, each aimed at a different adversary. Layer one addresses fraud and account takeover, the kind that actually costs people money: a password manager with a different password per site, two-factor authentication using the strongest method available, keeping the system and browser updated, and switching channel to confirm any message that pushes you to act quickly. It takes about an hour, starting with email, then banking and messaging accounts. Layer two addresses commercial data collection by platforms, advertisers and data brokers: phone permissions and the advertising identifier, full-disk encryption with a boot password, end-to-end encrypted messaging, backups that you have tested restoring, and an account inventory. Layer three addresses targeted investigation and is only needed in specific situations. The red box below lists six overrated measures: VPNs, private browsing, scheduled password changes, changing your phone number, camera stickers and deleting apps, each of which has a real use but is often mistaken for the main line of defence.
svg.text: This is the one that costs
A password manager, a different password per site
Two-factor authentication, the strongest method available
Keep the system and browser updated
Switch channel to confirm any message that rushes you
Phone permissions and the advertising identifier
Full-disk encryption and a boot password
Backups, and a restore you have actually tested
One item at a time, no need
to finish it in one sitting
See the section on when to raise your standard
Overrated measures: each has a use, none is the main line of defence
A VPN changes who can see your connection. Private browsing clears local traces while platforms and your ISP still recognise you.
NIST no longer asks for scheduled password changes. A recycled phone number gets reassigned, so unlink the old accounts first.
A camera sticker works on the camera, while most people are worried about the microphone. Deleting an app stops future collection only.
Put all your effort into the third adversary and the losses from the second still happen. The reverse holds too.
You do not have to finish all three at once. Layer one alone removes most of the loss from account takeover and fraud.
